cards.b: One melodic line only, with no accompaniment.
Parts moving together in chords, or a melody with chordal accompaniment.
Two or more independent melodic lines of equal importance together.
The same melody played at once with slight variations.
Strict imitation: the same melody enters in each part one after another.
A phrase answered by a different voice or instrument.
Main tune alternates with episodes: A B A C A.
Every verse has the same music.
No repeated sections; new music throughout.
A bass line repeated throughout with changing music above it.
A returning orchestral theme between solo episodes, as in Bach's Brandenburg 5.
A contrasting section of about eight bars late in a pop song.

short.q: Describe how the texture changes in a layered track that adds parts one at a time.
short.model: It starts thin with one part and thickens as each part enters until it is a full, thick texture.
Verses tell the story, with a repeated chorus; often with an intro, middle 8 and final chorus.

short.q: What happens in the development section of sonata form?
short.model: Themes from the exposition are altered and moved through different keys.
A melody or motif is repeated by another part soon after it first appears.
A bold recurring theme played by the full group, returning in different keys between solo episodes.
